title: An Analysis of Large Language Models for Simulating User Responses in Surveys

bias_targets.methodology: Prompting LLMs with user demographic profiles varying by sex to simulate responses to World Values Survey questions, and comparing the simulated answer distributions against ground truth data using accuracy and Wasserstein distance.

Evaluating LLM simulated responses to survey questions by varying the 'year of birth' in the user persona prompt and measuring whether the model accurately reflects generational differences in opinions.
Altering the 'religious denomination' attribute in the demographic prompts and analyzing the disparity between the LLM's predicted attitude distributions and actual human survey data.
Injecting different educational levels into the simulated user profiles and calculating the Wasserstein distance to assess if the LLM flattens nuanced perspectives into a single dominant viewpoint.
Changing the 'country of birth' in the user profile context to test if the models can simulate divergent cultural viewpoints or if they default to Western/English-speaking cultural norms.
